 Oral Judgment
(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE N.S.SANJAY GOWDA)
The Insurer as well as the claimants are in appeal challenging the compensation of `8,49,000/- awarded for the death of Mallamma.

The Insurer is in appeal basically contending that as per the evidence on record the husband of the deceased-Mallamma also passed away after filing of the claim petition and her unmarried daughter Anitha was also married after the death of Mallamma and the remaining sons being majors, there was no question of dependency and hence the order of the Tribunal is incorrect.

sentences.text: 3. The claimants on the other hand contend that the sums awarded were inadequate and the income assessed was on the lower side.

4. The argument of the Insurer that because the husband of the deceased passed away and the daughter was also subsequently married, coupled with the fact that the sons were majors, there was no question of dependency arise, cannot be accepted.
5. The husband of the deceased as well as the daughter of the deceased acquired a vested right to claim a compensation on the day Mallamma was killed in the accident.
If after they had instituted proceedings for NC: 2024:KHC-K:6903 recovering the claim, the husband were to die, his entitlement to claim compensation cannot evaporate.

The vested right that the husband has to secure compensation would continue on his legal heirs and they would be entitled to prosecute the same and succeed to that estate.
6.

It may also be pertinent to state here that the dependency of the husband and the minor daughter as on the date of the accident was definite and this element of dependency cannot be defeated by the subsequent death or marriage of claimant Nos.1 and 2.
7.
It is also to be noticed that the sons were aged between 21 to 25 years and therefore they would also be dependent on their mother at least to a limited extent.

The mother of three sons who were in their early twenties would definitely contribute to their well being and will be taking care of their needs, which also has a financial component and therefore their dependency cannot also be denied.
In this result, the argument of the Insurer cannot be accepted, the same as rejected.
9. As far as enhancement is concerned, it is noticed that the deceased was aged 42 years and the Tribunal has taken the notional income at `6,000/- per month.
Since there is no proof of actual income, the notional income of `8,000/- determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority which for the year 2015 will have to be applied.

10. As per the decision of the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs.
Pranay Sethi and Others1, as the deceased was aged about 42 years, 25% of the same (`2,000/-) is required to be added to the said income as future prospects and the resultant income would thus be `10,000/-.

sentences.text: 11. Out of the said sum, 1/3rd of the same (`3,333/-) would have to be deducted towards personal (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC: 2024:KHC-K:6903 expenses of the deceased, as she was survived by her husband and children.
The net income will be `6,667/-.

12. As the deceased was aged 42 years, as per the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another2, a multiplier of '14' would have to be applied.

sentences.text:
Consequently, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of `11,20,056/- (`6,667/- x 12 x '14')
towards "loss of dependency" as against `7,56,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

14. The claimants being the children of the deceased (claimant Nos.2 to 5), each of them would be entitled to a sum of `48,400/- towards loss of love and affection i.e., in all `1,93,600/- and a further sum of `36,300/- will have to be awarded under the conventional heads.

Thus, the claimants, in modification of the impugned award, would be entitled to the following sums :
 Sl. Compensation As awarded  Nature of Heads  No. by this Court (`)
 1. Loss of Dependency 11,20,056/-
 Loss of love and
affection

3. Conventional heads 36,300/-
 Total 13,49,956/-

16. Thus, the claimants would be entitled for compensation of `13,49,956/- as against `8,49,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal, along with interest at the rate of six per cent per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
17. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded along with interest within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
18. Consequently the appeal of the Insurer i.e., MFA No.200206/2017 is dismissed and the appeal filed NC: 2024:KHC-K:6903 by the claimants i.e., MFA No.201354/2018 is allowed in part.
19. The apportionment, deposit and release of the enhanced compensation amount shall be made as per the ratio adopted by the Tribunal.
20. The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal for disbursal in terms of the award.
